title: Test-Order Dependency (Shared Mutable Global State)
pattern: Tests that modify shared global variables, database records, static singletons, or environment contexts without isolating or resetting state in cleanup teardown routines.
why_bad: It violates test isolation (hermeticity) [507]. Tests become non-deterministic, flaky, and highly order-dependent [507]. It makes parallel execution impossible and causes confusing failures located far from the actual bug [331, 460].
detection: The presence of mutable static globals, file writes, environmental changes, or shared databases inside tests without accompanying `tearDown` or rollback blocks.
counterexample: Writing to a thread-local variable or an isolated, memory-allocated database instance configured uniquely per test case.
fix: Make each test hermetic by setting up its own environment locally [507]. If singletons must be used, introduce static setup/teardown setters (`setTestingInstance`) to reset state between runs [310, 620].
source:
*   *Software Engineering at Google*, "Properties common to all test sizes" (p. 218) [507]
*   *Working Effectively with Legacy Code*, "Introduce Static Setter / Static Cling" (p. 120-125, 372) [310, 331, 620, 653]
*   *A Philosophy of Software Design*, "Global variables" (p. 46) [460]
